subject: Azure Offer creation — validation runway & publisher account gaps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Azure Marketplace Validation <mpartner-validation@microsoft.com>, Serena Liu <serena.liu@corestream.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Azure Offer creation — validation runway & publisher account gaps

Hi Serena / Marketplace team,

Thanks for taking this on. CoreStream and Redwood are aligning to publish a SaaS offer (metered API + VM fallback) to the Azure Marketplace and kick off co-sell enablement. We want to lock the technical validation window and surface any publisher-account gaps now so we don't get blocked mid-validation.

High-level asks:
- Can you confirm minimum validation window length and typical lead time for a SaaS + VM offer?
- We need a list of exact Partner Center roles/flags required on the publisher account before validation.
- Any known failure modes around SKU mapping or managed identity permissions you commonly see?

Attachments: svc_manifest_draft.json (initial manifest), security_matrix_v1.xlsx (controls mapping).

Proposed timeline: validation window week of Aug 10, soft freeze on manifest by EOD Aug 5. Serena, can you confirm CoreStream is fine with that slot?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Azure Marketplace Validation <mpartner-validation@microsoft.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Serena Liu <serena.liu@corestream.com>
Cc: Marketplace PM <mpm@microsoft.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Offer creation — validation runway & publisher account gaps

Marissa / Serena,

Thanks for the note. We can target Aug 10 for a validation slot; please make sure the manifest and deployment samples are ready 3 business days prior. Typical validation for a mixed SaaS/VM offer is ~2 business days of testing plus follow-up fixes.

Quick checklist for Partner Center / publisher account readiness:
- Partner Center account must be in Active state and have a Global admin or Commercial Marketplace admin assigned.
- Subscription/Publisher settings: Enable commercial marketplace listing and co-sell (if you want co-sell flagging).
- Provide a test tenant / sample subscription to exercise ARM templates and SaaS endpoint flow.

Common issues we see: SKU name mismatches between manifest and Azure portal listing, missing service principal permissions for deployment scripts, and incorrect URL formats in the REST endpoint block.

Links: Validation guidance: https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Marketplace/ValidationHelp
If you want co-sell enabled, we'll need a signed co-sell agreement (DocuSign link shared in separate email).

Please upload the final manifest and a short runbook or smoke-test script to the Azure validation portal before Aug 7.

Regards,
Azure Marketplace Validation Team
mpartner-validation@microsoft.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-02T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Azure Offer creation — validation runway & publisher account gaps

Forwarding Azure's guidance. Quick internal plan so owners are clear: 

Action items (owners):
- Soojin: finalize manifest (SKU names, ARM templates) and push manifest v2 to thread (due EOD Aug 4).
- Rishi: complete and tighten security_matrix_v1.xlsx with required evidence (keys, audit logs, retention) and flag anything we need help from CoreStream on (due Aug 5).
- Marissa: confirm publisher account admin and request test tenant from CoreStream; schedule validation window once manifest v2 is uploaded.

Note: we should pre-check SKU naming to avoid the common mismatch issue Azure called out. Keep it minimal and consistent with the portal display name.

Jonas
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Azure Marketplace Validation <mpartner-validation@microsoft.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-03T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Offer creation — validation runway & publisher account gaps

Team / Azure,

Thanks — attaching manifest v2 (svc_manifest_v2.json) with SKU normalization and the corrected ARM template reference. I also added a note in the manifest about the managed identity scope used for provisioning.

Proposed validation window: Aug 10-11 (Pacific time). CoreStream confirmed internal availability for the slot but asked for a short smoke-test step list (I included a 6-step smoke test in the attached runbook link).

Core open question: does the validation process require the Partner Center account to have a commercial marketplace billing profile active, or is activation of the publisher account alone sufficient? If billing profile is required we'll need to escalate with CoreStream to populate that ahead of the validation slot.

Attachments: svc_manifest_v2.json

>

Thanks,

soojin.lee@redwood.ai

From: Azure Marketplace Validation <mpartner-validation@microsoft.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Serena Liu <serena.liu@corestream.com>
Date: 2027-08-04T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Offer creation — validation runway & publisher account gaps

Soojin / Marissa / Serena,

Confirming Aug 10-11 validation window. A couple of clarifications:
- Publisher account: Partner Center activation + a Commercial Marketplace billing profile is recommended prior to validation for SaaS offers that will bill through Marketplace. If you plan to use Bring-Your-Own-Subscription (BYOS) only, the billing profile is not required for validation but will be required prior to publishing.
- Test tenant: We can provide a sandbox subscription for the validation team. We'll email the tenant details to Serena separately.
- Pre-check: please ensure the manifest and runbook are uploaded to the validation portal by EOD Aug 7. We'll run an initial manifest linting check on Aug 8 and send a short report.

Validation docs: https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Marketplace/ValidationHelp

We'll wait for the manifest upload and an explicit confirmation from Marissa that the publisher account has the required admin role.

Regards,
Azure Marketplace Validation Team
mpartner-validation@microsoft.com
